summary: The team is in execution mode on the China-first global marketing push — launching the Intelligent China webpage and driving Asia Star and Intelligent China to top-five search/AI visibility within seven months — while juggling a Knowledge website redesign, the AACSB Global Impact Award submission, and a live Yili Group enquiry.
summaryDetail: The single most important thing right now is getting Intelligent China live and firing on all cylinders: the webpage launch, the email campaigns to own and partner networks, and Joseph's audience/prompt plan and customer profiles all need to land so the seven-month top-five ranking goal for Asia Star and Intelligent China stays on track, with US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) deliberately parked for the first quarter. This week's urgent items are the AACSB Global Impact Award application — approved unchanged and due for submission by Tian Xuefang, with Ira running it past Prof. Zhu Rui — and the Yili Group enquiry, which Jay is leading and Cao Yi is tracking as a likely digitalization custom program. On the Knowledge website redesign, the team has settled on keeping the two-menu structure and the current homepage look with menu-categorization tweaks, dispersing videos by topic rather than a standalone section, and surfacing BCI/BSI indices; Joseph needs to share the HTML concept and book a 30-minute feedback session so Joker can make the design changes. Looking ahead, Ira and Joseph need to review the Flow design PPT and the polished Dean Xiang transcript for the school PPT, the videos strategy meeting is set, Joseph must send updated Asia Start campaign reports to European colleagues, and Tian Xuefang needs to brief the photographer for Asia Start photography at the Beijing campus — all while the team clears the Outlook lockout by updating saved passwords across every device and confirming the backend unlock with JSB.

decisions.text: Stale saved passwords on devices caused repeated failed logins and account lockout; all devices must be updated.
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic across the site
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge menu and School menu) at the top
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the Knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the very top of the homepage
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as the top two programs to promote; US programs (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) are secondary.
Treat Berkeley as a possible third priority for testing overseas program interest, to be considered in the audit phase.
Focus initial efforts on China programs and put US partnerships on hold for the first quarter.
Prof. Tao accepted the invitation to speak at the CKGSB x EuroCham Shanghai APEC event on Nov 13
